## Description

The Python 3 program reads sequences \(A\) and \(B\) from standard input and reports whether at least two distinct selections of positions in \(A\) produce \(B\).

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — Standard input contains integers in the stated three-line format. The first line gives \(N\) and \(M\), the second gives the \(N\) values of \(A\), and the third gives the \(M\) values of \(B\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The lengths satisfy \(1 \le M \le N \le 200{,}000\). Every sequence value is between \(1\) and \(10^9\), inclusive.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — A selection matches \(B\) if it uses exactly \(M\) strictly increasing positions in \(A\) and the selected values equal \(B\) in order. Two matching selections are distinct if they differ in at least one position. Distinct selections may share positions.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — The program prints a single answer to standard output. It prints `Yes` when there are at least two distinct matching selections and `No` when there are zero or one.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — When \(M=N\), the answer is always `No` because there is only one possible selection of all \(N\) positions. When \(M=1\), the answer is `Yes` exactly when the sole value of \(B\) occurs at least twice in \(A\).

## Test suggestions

- Use the three supplied samples to check zero, one, and more than two matches under PRE-1 and PRE-2 against POST-1 and POST-2.
- Use \(A=(1,1,2)\) and \(B=(1,2)\) to check that exactly two matches sharing the final position produce `Yes` under POST-1 and POST-2.
- Check \(M=N=1\) with equal values, \(M=N=200{,}000\) with equal sequences, and \(M=1\) with the target appearing once and twice to exercise PRE-2 and POST-3.

## Unspecified behavior

Behavior for malformed input or values outside the stated constraints is unspecified.
